title: ROS Staining for Arabidopsis Using Green Fluorescent Stain
author: Magdalena M Julkowska
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.zksf4we

steps.title: Prepare and transfer seedlings
steps.instruction: Transfer seedlings from agar plates into a nutrient solution identical to the agar plate composition (excluding Dashin agar), using 24, 12, or 6 well-plates depending on seedling size.

steps.title: Wash seedlings
steps.instruction: Wash the seedlings using medium that does not contain DCF-DA.

steps.title: Sterilize and germinate seedlings
steps.instruction: Sterilize and germinate the seedlings, then transfer them to a stress medium (e.g., salt stress) following the 'Quantification of salt-induced changes in Root System Architecture in Arabidopsis' protocol (dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.zkqf4vw).

steps.title: Apply DCF-DA stain
steps.instruction: Add DCF-DA to the liquid medium to achieve a final concentration of 50 uM.

steps.title: Incubate samples
steps.instruction: Incubate the samples for 30 min with gentle shaking, ensuring the well plate is wrapped in aluminium foil to protect the light-sensitive DCF-DA.

steps.title: Image the stain
steps.instruction: Use fluorescence microscopy to image the stain using the specified bandpass filters.
